svg.text: K5b DIE CASSETTES — one tube station, loose dies
Each die is a loose dishwasher-safe cassette the handler drops into the one Ø 260 shelf aperture. The same press does every job.
10 cassette types · flange Ø 258 on a 6 mm ledge
dicer blade sets bought (6, 10 mm, wedger-corer)
no turret, no carousel, no shear gate
Onion layers are pushed through the blade grid;
6 × 6 mm dice fall straight into the pot.
Boiled potatoes go in with the skin; the flesh passes,
the skins stay on the plate and go to waste.
A whole cabbage is split into eighths on staggered
blades; the core is punched out along the axis.
One stroke pushes out one portion; the wire bow of
the knife cage cuts it off; P0 rounds it later.
A Rouladen slice on its tray is pressed flat with a
water film: 1.5 kN for 3 s, like a mallet's flat.
The foot strikes the cradle (50–100 N), it spreads;
egg drops into the slotted saucer, white drains.

g.text: 1/4 Load: the handler drops the cassette into the shelf aperture and fills the tube (or sets the piece on the anvil / cradle)
2/4 Approach: the crosshead foot comes down at 150 mm/s until it touches
3/4 Press: 50 mm/s; the force–travel curve is watched for each job (dice, mash, wedges, portion, flat slice, cracked egg)
4/4 Result falls straight into the vessel below; the cassette goes to the dishwasher after this one use
